newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's oil trade deficit rises 11.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru's oil trade deficit rises 11.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: Peru's oil trade deficit rose 11.4 percent to $347 million in 1996 compared with $311 million during the previous year, the Central Bank said Friday.
The bank said in its weekly report that the country's oil deficit in December reached $52 million, up 215.5 percent compared with November's gap of $16 million.
Peru posted an oil trade deficit of $29 million in December 1995, it said.
In 1996, oil and derivitives exports rose 46.3 percent to $353 million versus exports worth $241 million in 1995, the bank added.
Imports of oil totalled $700 million in 1996, up 26.7 percent from $553 million the prior year, it said.
In December, oil exports reached $20 million while imports jumped to $72 million compared with $20 million and $49 million respectively in December 1995.
Peru's oil trade deficit has risen in recent years as production has failed to keep pace with rising domestic demand.
